concepts.def: School subjects: les maths, le français, l'anglais, l'histoire, la géographie, les sciences, l'EPS (PE).
Timetable vocabulary: la rentrée (start of term), la récréation (break), la cantine (canteen), les devoirs (homework).
Giving opinions: 'J'aime...', 'Je déteste...', 'parce que c'est ennuyeux/intéressant/utile'.
Comparing subjects/teachers: plus...que (more than), moins...que (less than), aussi...que (as...as). E.g. 'plus difficile que'.
School uniform vocabulary and debate: porter un uniforme (to wear a uniform), un pantalon, une cravate, une chemise.
School rules: 'Il est interdit de...' (It is forbidden to...), 'Il faut...' (One must...). Used with infinitive verbs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Context 3: School Life, Studies and the World of Work — a core area of GCSE French.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Context 3: School Life, Studies and the World of Work brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Context 3: School Life, Studies and the World of Work.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which sentence means 'Maths is more difficult than English'?
options: Les maths sont plus difficiles que l'anglais.
Les maths est plus difficile que l'anglais.
Les maths sont moins difficiles que l'anglais.
Les maths plus difficile l'anglais.
les devoirs
la récréation
la cantine
la rentrée

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I study maths' in French?
options: All verbs take avoir.
J'étudie maths.
J'étudie des maths.
J'étudie les maths.

mcqs.q: Which verbs take 'être' as their auxiliary in the passé composé?
options: J'étudie des maths.
Just movement verbs - never reflexives.
Movement/state-change verbs (DR & MRS VAN DER TRAMP) and all reflexive verbs.
All verbs take avoir.

mcqs.q: How do you say 'I am eating bread' (some bread) in French?
options: All verbs take avoir.
Je mange le pain (which means 'the bread').
Je mange pain.
Je mange du pain.
